data.description:
# Intake Brief — Drive epic children in interactive Herdr panes

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` (`phase_drive`, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) runs each
child's fresh Pi session as a **headless subprocess**:

```
pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions
```

with `capture_output=True`. The operator therefore has:

- no view of the child session while it runs (only the parent's own progress
  lines and `wait_for_job` heartbeats);
- no ability to watch the agent work, scroll its transcript, or intervene when
  it stalls, hits an approval/question boundary, or loops;
- no evidence after a failure beyond a 5-line `_tail_lines(...)` summary of
  captured stderr/stdout;
- no per-child terminal artefact to point at during review.

An operator running an epic in Herdr already watches a grid of interactive
`π` TUI panes for other work. Drive should produce the same kind of pane —
one interactive Pi TUI session per child, opened as a sibling pane in the
caller's tab — so the epic runs *visibly*.

A headless-in-a-pane variant (option A: `pane split` + `pane run` +
exit-sentinel) was evaluated and rejected as insufficient: it shows log text,
not a browsable/typeable Pi TUI session, and offers no session-level state.

## Users

- **Operator / producer driving an epic from a Herdr-managed Pi session.**
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when I run `implement.py drive <epic>`, I
    want each child implemented in its own interactive Pi TUI pane inside the
    tab I invoked from, so I can watch progress, scroll the full transcript,
    and step in if a child stalls — without leaving my own session."
- **Reviewer / auditor.** *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want each child's
  session transcript to still be inspectable after drive finishes, so I can
  check what the agent actually did."

## Goal

`implement.py drive <parent>` opens **each** child's implementation session as
an interactive Pi TUI agent in a new pane split from the calling pane (same
tab), drives that pane's lifecycle to completion, and continues the existing
serial/blocking-order/parent-last loop — preserving session isolation,
worktree isolation, error isolation, and the recursion guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive
   runs `herdr pane split` from the invoking pane (no `tab create`, no
   `workspace create`) with `--cwd <child worktree>` and returns the new pane
   id from `.result.pane.pane_id`; the child Pi TUI is started in that pane via
   `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve
   --no-extensions` and prompted with `/skill:implement <child_id>` via
   `herdr agent prompt ... --wait`. Verified by a test that asserts the herdr
   CLI invocations (split/prompt/wait/close) and asserts no tab/workspace
   creation call is made.
2. **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child
   is determined by (a) `herdr agent wait <name> --until done|blocked` for the
   pane-side signal and (b) the existing `phase_parent` re-read of the work
   item's stage as the authoritative signal. Drive never assumes an
   interactive agent process exits when the work item completes. Tests cover
   the `done`, `blocked`, and timeout transitions.
3. **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent
   reports `blocked` (approval/question UI), drive stops the chain, records the
   child id and the pane id in the JSON report (`blocked_child`,
   `blocked_pane`), leaves the pane open for the operator, and emits actionable
   text naming the pane. Tested with a fake herdr runner.
4. **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once
   its child reaches a terminal stage and the child's session was clean, or
   (b) explicitly retained and reported (blocked/failed) — never leaked
   silently. Unit tests assert a close call per successful child and no close
   call for blocked/failed children.
5. **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when
   Herdr is detected (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a resolvable herdr binary) **and** the
   operator opted in (`--pane-sessions`, or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`).
   Otherwise the existing `_default_session_spawner` headless path is used
   unchanged. Tests cover herdr-absent, opt-out, and herdr-present paths.
6. **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process
   receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`,
   and does **not** inherit `PI_SESSION_ID` / `PI_SESSION_FILE` from the
   driving session (assert the constructed env / pane-split `--env` args and
   the `env -u` prefix). Recursion guard and per-child worktree enforcement
   continue to work inside the pane.
7. **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.**
   `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (and the existing per-child session bound
   `--max-child-sessions`) still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane,
   records `reason`, and stops the chain as today. Tested with a fake clock /
   fake herdr wait returning `timeout`.
8. **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is
   unchanged; an explicit `--focus` variant switches to each new child pane.
   Assert the flag passed to `pane split` in both modes.
9. **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and
   gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport: "pane" | "headless"`; the
   final summary lists panes retained for inspection. Tests assert the new
   fields and that existing fields are unchanged (no breaking change for
   consumers of the drive report).
10. **Docs.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (drive section) and
    `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 document: pane-per-child behaviour, the
    opt-in flag/env var, focus behaviour, blocked-child handling (which pane to
    look at, and that it is intentionally left open), and the headless fallback
    for non-Herdr/automated callers.
11. **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit;
    the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Design sketch (non-binding)

- Add `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env, verbose)`
  next to `_default_session_spawner`, returning the same
  `{"success", "returncode", "reason"}` shape plus `pane_id`.
- Extract herdr CLI calls into a small injectable helper (reuse the fail-open
  style of `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`; do not duplicate its `HERDR_BIN_PATH`
  resolution logic — reuse or import it) so tests fake the CLI boundary with
  no live Herdr.
- In `phase_drive`, select the spawner by transport: existing injection point
  (`spawn_session`) already allows tests to bypass either; the CLI path chooses
  pane vs headless from the opt-in + detection check.
- Agent naming: `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` (herdr names must match
  `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, unique among live agents) — truncation/validation
  must be tested.
- Pane labelling: on completion/failure, set the pane title via the existing
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` helper so the retained
  pane carries its verdict.

## Constraints

- Do not change the session-per-child rule (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52), worktree
  isolation, dependency ordering, or parent-advanced-last semantics — all live
  above the spawner.
- Do not change `_default_session_spawner` behaviour for automated callers
  (downtime worker, audit dispatch, CI): headless `pi -p` must remain the
  default outside Herdr.
- No edits to the repo-external Herdr agent skill or the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` files (herdr-managed).
- `herdr agent start` requires the pane to be at an interactive shell prompt;
  the implementation must handle `agent_not_ready` (retry within the existing
  timeout or fail with a reported reason), not crash.
- Herdr CLI failures must be fail-open at the boundary (recorded reason,
  chain stops cleanly) — never leave the epic in an unrecoverable state.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Loss of the process-exit completion signal.** An interactive TUI session
  does not exit when the work item completes, so completion must come from
  wl stage + `agent wait`. *Mitigation:* AC 2 makes `phase_parent` the
  authority (it already is) and `agent wait` only a fast-path; covered by tests.
- **Pane/session leakage.** Panes and interactive agents persist after drive
  ends. *Mitigation:* AC 4 explicit close-or-report rule, plus pane-title
  verdict marking for retained panes.
- **Serial drive + visible panes can be noisy.** One pane open at a time,
  closed on success. *Mitigation:* documented; failure/blocked panes retained
  deliberately.
- **Herdr API drift** (JSON shapes, kind list, name rules). *Mitigation:*
  single injected helper for CLI calls; parse ids defensively; fail open.
- **Approval prompts could block an unattended epic.** *Mitigation:* start
  with `--approve` and treat `blocked` as an explicit, reported stop (AC 3).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`,
  `_child_session_env`, `_default_session_spawner`, `_resolve_child_session_timeout`,
  `_resolve_pi_bin`, `_emit_phase_report`; `--max-child-sessions` and
  `--child-timeout` CLI flags; `spawn_session` injection point.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — deterministic orchestration tests with
  `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
  — spawer/env tests.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — fail-open Herdr CLI helper (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`,
  `pane list`/`pane rename`, status prefix/truncation, `update_pane_title`).
- Herdr CLI surface (verified against the installed binary): `pane split
  --current --direction right|down --cwd --env --no-focus`, `pane run`,
  `pane wait-output`, `pane read`, `pane close`, `pane rename`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> [-- args]`, `agent prompt
  <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`, `agent wait`, `agent get`,
  `agent list`, `agent read`. Caller context env: `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`.

## Appendix: decisions from the discovery conversation

- Transport choice: **option B** (interactive Pi TUI agent in a pane) over
  option A (headless `pi -p` run in a pane, exit-sentinel + `pane read`).
  Rationale recorded: option A shows log text only; B gives a browsable,
  typeable session and Herdr's lifecycle states, at the cost of replacing the
  process-exit completion signal with wl-stage + `agent wait` (AC 2).
- Opt-in rather than default: automated callers (downtime worker, audit
  dispatch, CI) have no Herdr and must keep the headless path (AC 5).
- Forked-decision for planning: whether to factor the herdr CLI boundary into a
  shared module (`skill/shared/`) or keep it local to `implement.py`; prefer
  reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either way.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child) — the headless drive this item extends.
- **SA-0MUWBHEEF002A6BO** — When running implement on a parent item implement
  all children — original one-invocation drive requirement.
- **SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52** — When implementing an epic start a new session for
  each child — session isolation rule that must be preserved.
- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — User-visible progress feedback during long-running
  waits — related observability work for drive runs.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion — reuse `herdr_pane.update_pane_title` for retained panes.
data.title: implement drive: run each epic child in an interactive Herdr pane (same tab)

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (drive timeout reconciliation).

Problem: when implement.py start runs from inside an already-existing worktree (the resume path used by every driven child session), Step 9 writes ImplementState.repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve()) — the worktree path, not the main checkout. phase_finish then calls _remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root) whose safety gate 1 refuses when resolved_path == repo_root (CRITICAL: REFUSE to remove the repository root ... This is the main working tree, not a worktree; Restored status=open).

Impact: every driven child leaks its worktree, finish exits non-zero and restores the item to open even though the commit was pushed — a false failure needing manual status fix; .worklog/worktrees accumulates orphans.

Expected: phase_start should persist the main checkout root (e.g. via _main_checkout_for(worktree) following the gitdir) so phase_finish can remove the worktree after a successful push.

Evidence: SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK finish (commit b11d0877d pushed to dev, finish reported failure, worktree left in place).
data.title: implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root

data.description:
Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.

## Problem

A full-project  run reports fixes that were never applied.

Observed on 2026-10-28 (SorraAgents @ dev):
- Report claimed `Auto-fixed: 8`, listing EXE005, ISC004, PLW1510 and RUF059 findings.
- `git status` afterwards showed **no source changes at all** (only the unrelated `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` scheduled-prompt timestamp).

Verified cause: those diagnostics are *not* auto-fixable (`ruff check --fix` reports `fix: null` for EXE005/PLW1510/RUF059 and `fix.applicability: unsafe` for ISC004).

## Root cause

`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output` (line ~113) converts **every** diagnostic in ruff's JSON output into a `fixed_findings` entry, without inspecting `item['fix']` or `item['fix']['applicability']`. `auto_fix_files` (line ~217) then sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0` and the report prints those as auto-fixes. Ruff emits all diagnostics (fixed and unfixed) in its JSON output, so the count is the number of *diagnostics seen*, not fixes applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output` has the same shape (counts every message; eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields are ignored).

## Expected behaviour

- Only count a finding as auto-fixed when the linter actually applied an edit: ruff `item['fix']` is not `None` **and** `fix.applicability == 'safe'` (the default for `--fix` without `--unsafe-fixes`).
- Unfixable/unsafe diagnostics should either be dropped or surfaced as *remaining* smells, so they still reach smell detection, REFACTOR comments and work items.
- `fixes_applied`, the summary's `auto_fixed` count and the human-readable report must agree with what actually changed on disk.
- Add a regression test: a file with only-unsafe / no-fix diagnostics must report `Auto-fixed: 0`, and a file with a safe fix must report `Auto-fixed: 1` and be changed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output` only records findings whose fix is present and safe.
2. A full-project run against a tree whose only diagnostics are unsafe/unfixable reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A tree with one safe fix reports `Auto-fixed: 1` and the file is modified on disk.
4. Unsafe/unfixable diagnostics are still represented in the `Remaining smells` section (or equivalent) rather than silently dropped.
5. New unit tests in `skill/refactor/tests/` cover both cases.
6. Existing `skill/refactor` tests pass.

## Notes

Discovered from the `/skill:refactor` full-scan scheduled run. The 8 flagged diagnostics are already tracked by open REFACTOR items (SA-0MVRCL0Q90016C7D, SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW, SA-0MVRBPY7J004GJAI, SA-0MVPTU9HG00146UV), so this item is only about report/labelling accuracy.
data.title: refactor skill reports false auto-fixes for unfixable linter diagnostics

2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.

## Goal

Five tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` are source-code-grep / structural anti-patterns (per `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). Rework them to assert observable behaviour, or delete them if the behaviour is already covered elsewhere. Discovered by the test-churn pruning review (analyser v2.1.0, dev @ 7875214).

## Affected tests (line numbers at discovery)

- L427 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents the audit gating step` — reads SKILL.md text, asserts word substrings.
- L462 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js imports checkAuditReadyToClose` — reads source text, asserts string presence (the import behaviour is already exercised by the module-import behaviour tests).
- L478 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js uses exit code 6 for audit gate failure` — reads source text, asserts `'return 6'`/similar. Behaviour should be verified by exercising run-release against a failing audit gate.
- L496 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents exit code 6 for audit gate` — includes a near-placeholder catch-all condition `(content.includes('6') && content.includes('audit'))` that matches almost any content.

The file is otherwise healthy (89 tests, 255 asserts, real behaviour via `await import(MODULE_PATH)` + `execFileSync`); the fix must not remove the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five tests above either pin observable behaviour (running the real module/gate and asserting output/exit codes) or are deleted.
- [ ] No test in the file reads a source or markdown file and asserts a substring of its text.
- [ ] The near-placeholder catch-all condition (L496) is eliminated.

## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report

data.description:
## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.
data.title: Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime

# plan/intake AC coverage review creates duplicate "Close coverage gap" children when covering children already exist

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — observed while running `/skill:plan`.

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py:apply_coverage_review` (`action: auto_close`) creates one child per *parent AC it judges uncovered*, with the AC text copied verbatim and the title `Close coverage gap: [ ] **ACn — …**`. On a parent whose six feature children each restate an AC in their own words, it judged **all five** ACs uncovered and created five thin `idea`-stage duplicates alongside the real children.

Observed on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`:

- Six properly-formed children existed (config+guard, docs, three AC-verification children, validation) before the review ran.
- `apply_coverage_review(..., target_stage='plan_complete')` returned `action: auto_close` and created `MS-0MVTEXGU6007Z48U`, `MS-0MVTEXH6F008DVJF`, `MS-0MVTEXHK8002E376`, `MS-0MVTEXHWT0074M3M`, `MS-0MVTEXI9G002ROD0` (AC1–AC5).
- A follow-up `run_coverage_review` then reported `coverage_pct: 100` — mapping each parent AC **only** to the newly created gap child, i.e. the review's own output became its evidence.
- Resolution taken: all five were closed as duplicates with a comment mapping each AC to its real covering child, and the parent recorded the outcome.

## Why it matters

- The review silently degrades a well-planned tree (6 children) into 11, half of them AC-text stubs with no key files, constraints or evidence requirement — the opposite of what the review is meant to enforce.
- The "coverage" metric measures lexical similarity between the parent AC text and child AC text, not whether the child actually discharges the AC, so a correctly reworded child scores as a gap.
- Closing the duplicates afterwards leaves the parent at `plan_complete` with the tool's mapping invalidated, so a later re-run is ambiguous (re-create the stubs, or report gaps?).

## Suggested direction

- Before creating a gap child, require a **semantic/structural** match — e.g. child AC coverage by the parent's AC identifier (`AC1`, `AC2`, …, tolerant of reworded text) or by an explicit `Covers: ACn` line in the child description — and skip creation when matched.
- Treat `parent AC -> child` mapping as evidence only when the child has a non-stub body (ACs + Key Files/evidence), and prefer reporting `stop` with the specific unmatched ACs over creating thin children.
- Make the post-`auto_close` mapping exclude the auto-created children themselves when reporting `coverage_pct` (no self-satisfying evidence).
- Cover the case with a test: parent with 5 ACs, 5 reworded covering children → `action: proceed`, no children created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parent whose ACs are all covered by existing children — including children that reword the AC text — yields `action: proceed` and creates **zero** children.
- [ ] Gap children are created only when no child declares or demonstrably discharges the AC; the created child still restates the AC verbatim (current behaviour preserved for genuine gaps).
- [ ] `coverage_pct` never counts a gap child created by the same review as coverage for its own AC.
- [ ] Unit test(s) cover: fully-covered-with-reworded-AC → proceed; genuinely uncovered AC → auto_close with exactly one child; idempotent re-run creates no duplicates.
- [ ] `plan`/`intake` SKILL.md text states how coverage is matched, so agents can declare coverage (`Covers: ACn`) instead of relying on wording.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `run_coverage_review`, `apply_coverage_review`, AC extraction/matching.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — the documented coverage step.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tests/` — coverage-review unit tests.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** — the planning session where this was observed (children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W`, `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA`, `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`).
data.title: Coverage review creates duplicate gap children for already-covered ACs (reworded child ACs score as gaps)

## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
data.title: Carry the accepted-variance and push-gate conventions into templates/project-AGENTS.md

# implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`implement.py start` initialises submodules *after* it creates the
`node_modules` symlinks. When a submodule's own root has a `node_modules` in
the main checkout (tce-the-rising's `core` submodule does), the nested-symlink
pass creates `<worktree>/core/node_modules` inside the still-**empty**
submodule directory. `git submodule update --init` then cannot clone into
`core/` and fails:

```
fatal: clone of 'file:///home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine' into submodule path '…/core' failed
fatal: destination path '…/core' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

Because submodule init failures are deliberately fail-open (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ
AC2), `start` only logs a warning and the session proceeds with an
**uninitialised submodule**: `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit`) then dies with
`Cannot find module './core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin'`,
`@core-engine/SaveLoad`, etc. Every child session in that worktree must
hand-fix the checkout before it can build.

Secondary defect: even after a successful init, the symlink is not ignored by
the submodule's `.gitignore` (`node_modules/` has a trailing slash, which does
not match a *symlink*), so the superproject reports `M core` and the worktree
looks dirty.

## Evidence

- Call order in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (start phase):
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (≈L4608) → `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`
  (≈L4614) → `_ensure_submodules` (≈L4618).
- Observed on tce-the-rising worktree
  `wl-RISE-0MVRZKINX004HNEE-…`: `git submodule status` showed
  `-19f30ac… core` (uninitialised) while `core/` contained only the
  `node_modules` symlink; the first `npm run build` produced ~40 `TS2307`
  errors from the missing submodule.
- Manual fix that worked: `rm core/node_modules && rmdir core`,
  `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init --recursive`,
  re-create `core/node_modules`, and add `node_modules` to the submodule's
  `info/exclude` (the trailing-slash pattern in `core/.gitignore` does not
  match the symlink).

## Required change

- Run `_ensure_submodules` **before** the node_modules symlink passes, or make
  the nested-symlink pass skip paths that are inside an
  uninitialised/unchecked-out submodule (a gitlink with an empty directory).
- Make the worktree's `git status` clean after the symlinks are created: drop
  or neutralise the symlink's untracked status (e.g. immediately cover it by
  an exclude entry, or create the nested link only after init and add the
  path to the worktree's exclude).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose submodule root has a `node_modules` in the main checkout is
  fully initialised by `start`: `git submodule status` in the worktree shows a
  checked-out submodule (no leading `-`) and the repo's build succeeds.
- Ordering regression test: fixture repo with a local-path submodule plus a
  `<submodule>/node_modules` in the main checkout → after `start`, the
  submodule is checked out at the recorded commit and the worktree
  `git status --porcelain` is clean.
- The fail-open contract is unchanged: a genuinely failing
  `git submodule update` still only logs a warning and does not abort `start`.
- No behavioural change for repos without submodules or without a submodule
  `node_modules`.
- `implement/SKILL.md` submodule section notes the ordering constraint.

## Constraints

- Do not remove the node_modules symlinking feature itself
  (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) — only fix its ordering/ignoring relative to
  submodules.
- Keep the change generic; no tce-the-rising / `core`-specific hardcoding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_submodules`,
  `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, start-phase call order.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — ordering/regression test next to
  `test_implement_submodules.py`-style fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — submodule documentation.
data.title: implement.py start: nested node_modules symlink blocks submodule init (bootstrap ordering)

# Refactor: replace five `# noqa: F811` suppressions with one explicit fixture re-export in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Problem statement

The refactor scan filed this item as a critical `unused_import` finding (ruff `F811`, "Redefinition of unused `implement_mod`") against a worktree copy of `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`. That finding has **already been silenced** — commit `c39cb4454` added five line-scoped `# noqa: F811 — fixture param, not a redefinition` comments — so `ruff check` on `dev` is currently clean. What remains is the suppression noise itself: five separate "this is not a redefinition" assertions, each attached to a different line in the same file, when the intent belongs at exactly one place — the import. A single explicit re-export at the import site expresses that intent once and removes all five suppressions.

## Users

- **Test maintainer / agent** editing `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`: wants the fixture-sharing intent stated once, at the import, instead of re-verified against five inline suppressions.
- **Code reviewer / audit agent**: wants ruff clean without suppressions that require per-line re-justification.
- **Future test author** borrowing another test module's fixture: wants a precedent in this repo for re-exporting a fixture cleanly.

User stories:

- As a test maintainer, I want the fixture re-export declared once at the import so that the five `# noqa: F811` comments can be deleted without ruff complaining.
- As a reviewer, I want the lint result to stay clean when the suppressions are removed, so trust in the lint gate is preserved.
- As a future test author, I want a documented pattern for reusing a fixture defined in another test module.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` imports the fixture with an explicit re-export alias (`implement_mod as implement_mod`) and the file contains **zero** `# noqa: F811` comments — verify: `grep -c "noqa: F811" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` returns `0`, and `grep -n "implement_mod as implement_mod" tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` returns the import line.
2. The repo lint gate reports no findings for this file and no new findings elsewhere — verify: `ruff check tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` reports zero findings, and the gate's own entry point (`from code_review.scripts.linter_runner import run_ruff`, as used by the code-review tests) returns no findings for this path.
3. Every existing test in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` passes **unchanged** (no test-logic edits in this item), proving pytest still discovers the re-exported `implement_mod` fixture — verify: that module's tests are green in the changed-scope run.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (the module docstring/comment explaining fixture reuse), README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-neutral refactor.** Only the import statement and the five suppression comments change; no production code, no test logic, no fixture semantics.
- **Do not relocate fixtures** into `tests/conftest.py` (or a shared fixtures module) as part of this item — that is a larger, higher-blast-radius change. Record it as a linked follow-up if it looks worthwhile.
- The explicit re-export must be accompanied by a short explanatory comment so the `as x as x` idiom is not mistaken for redundant code.
- Keep the diff limited to `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`.

## Existing state

- Finding origin: refactor scan of the now-deleted worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND-tests-drive-recovery-test-harness-termin/` (the ephemeral path is dead; the live file is `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py:57-62` imports `PARENT`, `RecordingSpawner`, `ScriptedParent` and `implement_mod` from `tests/test_implement_drive.py`; `implement_mod` currently carries `# noqa: F401 — re-exported as a pytest fixture`.
- Five `# noqa: F811 — fixture param, not a redefinition` suppressions exist at lines 285, 649, 673, 687 and 884 (the fixture parameter shadowing the import).
- `ruff check tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` on `dev` passes today (single repo-wide suppressions are the only reason F811 does not fire).
- Verified locally with `ruff 0.16.0`: changing the import to `implement_mod as implement_mod` (with no `noqa`) and deleting all five `# noqa: F811` comments still yields `All checks passed!` under `--select F401,F811`.

## Desired change

Replace the fixture import with an explicit re-export and delete the five suppressions:

```python
from tests.test_implement_drive import (
    PARENT,
    RecordingSpawner,
    ScriptedParent,
    # Explicit re-export (``x as x``): registers the fixture for this module
    # without F401/F811 suppressions at each use site.
    implement_mod as implement_mod,
)
```

and drop `# noqa: F811 — fixture param, not a redefinition` (and the shorter `# noqa: F811 — fixture param`) from the five parameter sites, leaving trailing whitespace trimmed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — import block (~lines 57-62) and the five suppression sites (285, 649, 673, 687, 884); the only file expected to change.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — defines the `implement_mod` fixture; read-only reference.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `run_ruff` (imported as `code_review.scripts.linter_runner`), the lint path used by the code-review/refactor gates; read-only reference for AC2.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND** (Tests: drive recovery test harness + terminal regression, completed) — created this test file and applied the `# noqa: F811` fix in commit `c39cb4454` ("Ruff F811 noqa fix applied during handover"). Its acceptance criteria are fully satisfied; this item only narrows to the residual suppression cleanup.
- **SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY** — the drive bounded-recovery epic that owns the file's behaviour.
- **SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK** (quality improvement epic) — parent of a comparable earlier F811 refactor item (`SA-0MUMY6MEZ001EIW3`, `run_tests.py`), useful precedent for how these findings were resolved.

## Risks and assumptions

- **A1 — narrowing rather than closing.** The original `F811` is already suppressed, so a strict duplicate-work reading would close this item. This brief instead narrows it to the remaining gap (suppression noise). If the producer prefers no work at all, close the item instead of implementing.
- **A2 — re-export idiom.** `x as x` is the recognised pyflakes/ruff re-export idiom; verified locally that it silences both `F401` and `F811` for this file.
- **R1 — fixture discovery regression.** Changing the import could in principle stop pytest resolving `implement_mod`. Mitigated by keeping the bound name identical; AC3 (existing tests green, unmodified) is the guard. No *new* "fixture resolves" test is added — that would duplicate existing coverage.
- **R2 — unrelated repo-wide ruff findings.** Running the repo-wide lint gate may surface findings unrelated to this item; those are out of scope and belong in separate refactor items (the scan files them itself).
- **R3 — scope creep.** Tempting cleanups (moving shared fixtures to `tests/conftest.py`, renaming `implement_mod`) must be recorded as linked follow-up items, not absorbed here.
- **A3 — priority.** The refactor scanner set `high` from the original "critical" severity; once the finding is understood as already-suppressed noise, `low` matches the repo's priority guide (cosmetic/polish, no functional impact). This brief assumes `low`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** The seed context (a linter finding with file, line, rule code and message) plus repository inspection was sufficient to determine both that the finding is already resolved and what residual work remains. All decisions were therefore recorded as documented assumptions (A1–A3) rather than blocking questions.
- Q: "Is the reported `F811` still live on `dev`?" — Answer (agent, repo evidence): "No. `ruff check tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` passes on `dev`; commit `c39cb4454` added the five suppressions." Source: `git show c39cb4454`, local ruff 0.16.0 run.
- Q: "Does the original file path still exist?" — Answer (agent, repo evidence): "No. The worktree `wl-SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND-…` has been removed; the live file is `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` in the main checkout." Source: `find`/`ls` of `.worklog/worktrees/`.
- Q: "Can the suppressions be removed without reintroducing the finding?" — Answer (agent, repo evidence): "Yes — `implement_mod as implement_mod` plus deletion of all five `# noqa: F811` comments passes `ruff check --select F401,F811`." Source: scratch copy linted with ruff 0.16.0.
- **Duplicate-work check performed**: searched `test_implement_drive_recovery`, `F811`, `implement_mod`, `redefinition`, `fixture`; the only overlapping item is `SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND` (completed), which already delivered the suppression. This item is therefore narrowed (partial overlap) rather than closed.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVLJXKB60088SND** – Tests: drive recovery test harness + terminal regression (completed)
- **SA-0MQEEOK5N003ILYB** – [CRITICAL] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py:963 — Local variable `file_paths_in_findings` is assigned to but never used (F841) (completed)
- **SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C** – Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for parent/drive (open)

### Repository file matches
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — the file this item refactors (five `# noqa: F811` sites).
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — defines the `implement_mod` fixture being re-exported.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `run_ruff`, the lint path that raises/tolerates the finding.

*(Automated matches for `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` were dropped manually: the keyword extractor matched intake-brief scaffolding terms (`ac2`, `acceptance`, …), not the subject of this item.)*
data.title: Refactor: replace five noqa F811 suppressions with one explicit fixture re-export in tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py

# `implement.py parent`/`drive` start children whose status is `blocked` — re-validate the block before starting or skipping

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — producer decision Q3 (2026-10-29): *"yes, though it should first check that the block is still valid"*.

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent`/`drive` to never start a child that is deliberately `blocked` unless the block no longer holds, so a verification child is not implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and I am not asked to fabricate its evidence.

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` classifies children with `_classify_child()` (`implement/scripts/implement.py:874`): terminal → `skip-terminal`, `in-progress` → `skip-in-progress`, **everything else → `implement`**. Status `blocked` therefore falls through to `implement`.

Blocker awareness exists but does not gate the start:

- `_in_chain_blockers()` only considers blockers that are **themselves children of the same parent** (`implement.py:5920-5975`), so a child blocked on anything outside the parent's children set is startable.
- `external_blockers` is populated from outbound `wl dep` edges only (`implement.py:5771-5790`) and is reported as a "coordination note". It is `[]` when the block is recorded in prose instead of as a dependency edge — which is how cross-project blocks are written (`**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` in the child description).

**Live evidence (this item's origin):** on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — status `blocked`, unblock condition "`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` is in `dev`/`in_review`", which was still `open`/`intake_complete` — created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`. The child had to be aborted (`implement.py abort`, worktree removed) to avoid producing unverifiable AC evidence.

The inverse failure matters too: a **stale** block must not strand a child forever. Once the blocker lands, the child must become startable again (or its status refreshed) rather than being skipped silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block still holds: `_classify_child()` (or the caller) yields a distinct `skip-blocked` outcome, and the child is reported in `children_processed` with its blocking ids — not started, not `skipped-in-progress`.
- [ ] **Re-validation of dependency-edge blocks:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`) or soft-deleted, in which case the child is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log). Any non-terminal blocker holds the block.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line (and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented) are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers`; an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated — it must not default to startable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary.
- [ ] Node and pytest suites green for the changed framework code (run through the test skill / finish gate, never an ad-hoc runner).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing guards: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, "never re-implement terminal children", "never clobber another agent's `in_progress` claim", and `--finalise-stranded` semantics stay as they are.
- No change to `implement.py start`/`finish` single-item behaviour; this is the parent/`drive` fan-out classification only.
- Cross-project resolution must stay fail-open in the sense that an unresolvable id reports clearly and does not crash the phase — it just holds the block.
- Prose parsing must not become the only mechanism: prefer declared dependency edges, and keep the prose path narrowly scoped to an explicit `Blocked by` line.

## Key Files

- `implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child()`, `phase_parent()` (child classification, `_in_chain_blockers`), `phase_drive()` (report propagation), `wl_dep_blockers()`.
- `implement/scripts/tests/` (or the repo's existing implement test location) — new unit tests for the classification matrix.
- `implement/SKILL.md` — Guards + parent recursion report vocabulary.
- Reference cases: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` children `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (all `blocked`, blockers in prose).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`, `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — the three blockers of the origin item's verification children.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; this item makes them gate the start.

---

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-30)

**Headline:** Split the fix into a test-first contract item, three vertical
behaviour slices (classification → prose/cross-project blockers → drive
reporting), a docs item and a live-evidence item, all under this parent, with
every parent AC mapped to a child.

### Child work items (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Id | Title | Type | Effort/Risk |
|---|----|-------|------|-------------|
| C1 | `SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C` | Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for parent/drive | task | M / Medium |
| C2 | `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW` | phase_parent: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation) | feature | M / Medium |
| C3 | `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB` | Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a blocked child | feature | M / Medium |
| C4 | `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5` | phase_drive: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids | feature | S / Low |
| C5 | `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO` | Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary | docs | XS / Low |
| C6 | `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF` | Live evidence: `parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` starts no blocked child | task | S / Medium |

Dependency edges (all wired with `wl dep add`):

```
C1 (tests, no blockers)
 └─ C2 ─┬─ C3 ─┬─ C4 ─┬─ C5 (docs)
        │      │      └─ C6 (live evidence)
        └──────┴────────┘
```

Ordering rationale: C1 writes the red contract first (parent AC 5); C2 lands
the dep-edge verdict (AC 1, 2, 4-dep-path); C3 adds the prose/cross-project
path (AC 3, 4-prose-path) and makes the fail-closed default actionable; C4
propagates the verdict through `drive` (AC 1 "reported in `children_processed`"
on the drive path); C5 documents the shipped vocabulary (AC 7); C6 produces the
live evidence (AC 6). Each slice is end-to-end: code + tests + the finish gate.

### Parent AC → child coverage

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 `skip-blocked` distinct outcome, reported in `children_processed` with blocking ids | C2 (classification + report), C4 (drive propagation), C1(a) |
| AC2 dep-edge re-validation, stale iff every blocker terminal/soft-deleted | C2, C1(b) |
| AC3 prose `Blocked by` / cross-project ids surfaced in `external_blockers`; unresolvable holds with an actionable message | C3, C1(c) |
| AC4 unvalidatable block holds and is reported unvalidated | C2 (no dep edges), C3 (no parseable line) |
| AC5 unit tests (a)–(e) | C1 |
| AC6 live evidence on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` | C6 |
| AC7 `implement/SKILL.md` Guards + report vocabulary | C5 |
| AC8 node + pytest suites green through the test skill / finish gate | every child's finish gate; stated explicitly in C1 and C2 |

### Assumptions (recorded, not invented requirements)

- **A1 — test location.** The Key Files section above predicted
  `implement/scripts/tests/`; the repo's existing implement tests live in
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` at the repo root, so C1 creates
  `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` there.
- **A2 — prose only, no schema change.** AC3's "and/or a machine-readable
  `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by parsing
  the explicit `Blocked by …` line plus declared dependency edges; no `wl`
  schema change (wl is a separate ContextHub-owned CLI).
- **A3 — cross-project ids are resolvable in principle.** `implement.py`
  already routes `wl` calls through
  `shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`, whose prefix-to-sibling scan
  maps an id prefix to its owning project's worklog. Verified on 2026-10-30:
  from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`, prefix `SA` resolves to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` and `MS` to the tce worklog.
  Whether C3 *uses* that to detect a landed cross-project blocker is Q3 below.
- **A4 — one existing test encodes the superseded contract.**
  `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`
  asserts that a `blocked` child with an out-of-chain blocker **is started**
  ("coordination notes" per `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`). This item deliberately
  supersedes that behaviour; C1 updates and renames the test rather than
  leaving two contradictory contracts.
- **A5 — legacy helper kept.** `_next_child_to_implement()` has no production
  call site (only `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`); C2 keeps it
  consistent with the new rule instead of deleting it (dead code is reported,
  not removed, in a bug-fix slice).
- **A6 — the live-evidence run can start something.** The origin epic's AC1
  child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is `open` (not `blocked`) with
  `assignee: Map` + tag `do-not-delegate`; `phase_parent` honours neither
  (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`). See Q1.
- **A7 — `blocked` status writes are unreliable.** `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`
  (ContextHub) records `wl update --status blocked` reporting success while the
  stored status reverted to `open`; the classification must therefore never
  depend on the framework being able to *write* `blocked`.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 — initial plan: 6 children created (`SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C`,
  `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW`, `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB`, `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5`,
  `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO`, `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`), 11 dependency edges wired,
  six automated review stages run, AC coverage verified at 100 %.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (2026-10-30, plan skill, downtime dispatch — **no interactive
producer available**; questions recorded here and flagged for producer review).

- **Q1 — What is the scope of the live-evidence AC (AC6)?**
  The origin epic `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` now has **three** `blocked` children
  (`MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`) and one
  **`open`** child (`MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`) held only by `assignee: Map` + the
  `do-not-delegate` tag. `phase_parent` honours neither assignee holds nor
  `do-not-delegate` (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so the
  post-fix run will still start that open child — while AC6 as written says the
  run "starts nothing".
  Options: **(A)** scope AC6 to "none of the three `blocked` children is
  started, all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids", and report
  the open held child truthfully with a cross-reference to
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`; **(B)** widen this item to also gate on
  `do-not-delegate`/assignee holds (overlaps `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, which is
  already planned and blocked); **(C)** prove the behaviour on a synthetic
  fixture epic in this repo and record the MS run as pending until
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.
  **Recommended:** A — it proves exactly the bug this item owns (a `blocked`
  child is never started) without duplicating the do-not-delegate item, and
  keeps the live evidence honest about what the run did.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  decides whether C6 (`SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`) can be executed at all, and
  whether the MS epic stays held after this fix lands.

- **Q2 — When a block is found stale, should the child's lifecycle status be
  refreshed, or only the start allowed?**
  AC2 says the child "is startable again (and the stale block is named in the
  report/log)"; the Goal paragraph adds "(or its status refreshed)".
  Options: **(A)** start the child and report/log the stale block, leaving the
  `blocked` status to the lifecycle owner (a comment on the child records the
  stale finding); **(B)** also flip the child to `open` via `StatusLifecycle`
  with an audit comment before starting; **(C)** flip to `open` and clear the
  prose `Blocked by` line.
  **Recommended:** A — it never silently erases a producer-set hold, it keeps
  `phase_parent` a reader of lifecycle state rather than a writer of it, and
  `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` shows blocked-status writes are unreliable in `wl`.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  determines whether C2 mutates child status (and therefore whether it needs
  the `StatusLifecycle` audit-comment path).

- **Q3 — Should a cross-project prose blocker be resolved through the sibling
  worklog scan (so a landed external blocker makes the block stale)?**
  `resolve_worklog_flags` already maps an id prefix to its owning project's
  worklog (verified for `SA` → SorraAgents and `MS` → tce-main-street), so
  resolution is technically available without any network call.
  Options: **(A)** resolve cross-project ids through that scan: terminal →
  stale (child startable), non-terminal → holds, and only a genuinely
  unresolvable id holds as unvalidated; **(B)** do not resolve cross-repo —
  every cross-project id holds, and the child's owner must refresh the child
  when the external item lands; **(C)** resolve opportunistically (try the
  scan, fall back to holds) but never cache the result.
  **Recommended:** A — it is what makes the origin epic self-unblocking when
  the three `SA-…` items land, which is the inverse failure the Goal names
  ("a stale block must not strand a child forever"); B leaves three MS
  children stranded forever and contradicts that Goal.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  changes C3's acceptance criteria (and its tests) materially.

All three questions are recorded on this item as a comment and the item is
flagged `needsProducerReview`. Planning itself is complete and independent of
the answers; only C6 (Q1), the status-refresh behaviour in C2 (Q2) and the
cross-project resolution in C3 (Q3) depend on them.
