## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 43 of the 44 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming already used by `tests/unit`) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).
data.title: Changed-scope test selection ignores test-*.mjs node suites

# `phase_parent`: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation)

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Test-first sibling: **C1** (blocked-child classification matrix).

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent` to never
start a child whose `status` is `blocked` while its block still holds, and to
re-evaluate (not honour forever) a **stale** block, so a verification child is
never implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and a landed
prerequisite never strands its dependent.

## Context

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  returns `implement` for `status: blocked`. Precedence today:
  terminal → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `implement`.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) builds `classifications` with
  `action`/`external_blockers` and gates the start only on **in-chain**
  blockers (`_in_chain_blockers`, blockers that are themselves children of the
  same parent, ~line 6787). `_next_child_to_implement()` (~line 1227) is a
  second, legacy classification path kept consistent by tests.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` → `outbound` entries with `id` and `status`
  (`wl_dep_blockers`, ~line 565).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `blocked` child whose block still holds yields a **distinct** classification (`skip-blocked`, i.e. `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`) from `_classify_child()` (or its caller); it is never `implement`, `skip-in-progress` or `skipped-terminal`. Precedence is explicit and documented: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] **Dep-edge re-validation:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, reusing `_is_terminal_status` / soft-delete semantics) — in which case the child is startable again and the stale block is named in the report (a `stale_blocks` entry, and a log/comment line naming the blocker ids). Any **non-terminal** blocker holds the block.
- [ ] `children_processed` entries for a held child carry `action: "skip-blocked"`, the child id, its status and `blocking_ids` (the ids that hold it); the report also lists them in `blocked_children` so `phase_drive`'s existing propagation keeps working.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated (`unvalidated_blocks`) — it must not default to startable. (The prose/cross-project resolution that makes such a child actionable lands in C3; until then the fail-closed behaviour is the correct default.)
- [ ] A `blocked` child with at least one terminal blocker **and** one non-terminal blocker still holds (the non-terminal one wins); a `blocked` child whose blockers are all soft-deleted is stale/startable.
- [ ] `_next_child_to_implement()` (legacy helper, still covered by `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`) applies the same rule so the two classification paths cannot diverge; it is kept, not deleted.
- [ ] Unchanged: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, terminal children never re-implemented, `skipped-held` precedence, `skip-in-progress` never clobbering another agent's claim, `--finalise-stranded` semantics, and single-item `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- [ ] The C1 tests for cases (a), (b) and (e) are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`) and the full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Minimal implementation sketch

- Add `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD` (~line 213).
- New helper, e.g. `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers) -> {"action", "blocking_ids", "stale_ids", "unvalidated"}`, called from `_classify_child`'s callers (`phase_parent`, `_next_child_to_implement`) with the child's outbound edges — `_classify_child` itself has no edge data, so either widen its signature with an optional `blockers` argument (defaulting to `None` → unvalidated/fail-closed) or keep the status test in `_classify_child` and resolve the blocked verdict in the callers. Prefer the smallest change that keeps both call sites consistent.
- Extend the `classifications`/`child_results` entries and the "no startable child" message to name the blockers.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken existing guards; do not change `start`/`finish` single-item behaviour.
- Prefer declared dependency edges over prose; no `wl` schema change, no `gh`/network calls.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child` (~1127), `_next_child_to_implement` (~1227), `phase_parent` (~6609, incl. `_in_chain_blockers` ~6787), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`_is_terminal_status` (~1082).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1's matrix (red to green).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes (superseded here).
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status; distinct, do not implement here.
- `SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J` — terminal blockers still gate topological ordering; distinct.

# Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a `blocked` child

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** (`skip-blocked` classification); test-first contract in **C1** (case (c)).

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need a blocker that is declared in the child's
description (the cross-project convention) to gate the start exactly like a
dependency edge, so a verification child is never started against an
unlanded prerequisite in another repository and the report tells me which id
to check and where.

## Context

- Cross-project blocks are written in prose, e.g. on
  `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`:
  `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** \`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2\` — *Finish gate: …* (in progress; …)`
  followed by an `**Unblock condition:**` line. `wl dep list` on that child
  returns `outbound: []`, so today the phase reports `external_blockers: []`
  and starts it.
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description`, so
  no extra fetch is needed to parse it.
- Ids in this worklog look like `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` / `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`;
  ids belonging to another repository's worklog are **not** resolvable from
  this one (`wl show` fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A narrowly scoped parser extracts blocker ids from an **explicit** `Blocked by …` line only (case-insensitive, tolerating the bold/labelled form `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):**` and a plain `Blocked by:`); it must not treat arbitrary prose, `Unblock condition:` text or `Related work` ids as blockers.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers` (id + resolvable status, or `unresolved`); an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable. The merged set gates the start via C2's `skip-blocked` verdict.
- [ ] **Resolvable** prose blocker (present in this worklog): terminal → stale (child startable, blocker named); non-terminal → holds, reported with its status.
- [ ] **Unresolvable** (cross-project / unknown) prose blocker → **holds**, and the report/message names the id plus where to check it (e.g. "check the owning project's worklog", with the id's prefix as the hint). Never silently ignored, never silently startable.
- [ ] A `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line is reported as **unvalidated** and holds (fail-closed) — never defaults to startable.
- [ ] Parsing never crashes the phase (fail-open on the parser, fail-closed on the verdict): a malformed line yields "unvalidated" rather than an exception.
- [ ] No `wl` schema change and no new machine-readable field: prose + declared dep edges only (the parent AC's "and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by this choice). Cross-project ids are not resolved over the network.
- [ ] C1 cases (c) and the fail-closed case are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Assumptions (recorded on the parent)

- A cross-project block can therefore never go stale automatically: when the
  external item lands, the child's owner must refresh the child (status
  `open`, or remove/annotate the `Blocked by` line). This is the fail-closed
  behaviour the parent's AC 3 asks for and is recorded as an assumption.

## Constraints

- Prose parsing must stay narrowly scoped (one explicit line); declared
  dependency edges remain the preferred mechanism.
- Do not weaken C2's fail-closed default, existing guards or single-item
  `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — blocked-child state helper from C2, `phase_parent` classification/reporting (~6609), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `wl_show_children` (~525).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1 matrix (case (c), fail-closed).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges; distinct.
- `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) — origin epic whose `blocked` verification children use the prose convention; the live-evidence item `C6` exercises it.

# `phase_drive`: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** and **C3**; test-first contract in **C1** (case (d)).

## Goal

As a dispatcher running `implement.py drive <epic>` unattended, I need the
drive report to carry the same blocked-child verdicts as `parent` — with the
blocking ids — so no session is spawned for a `blocked` child and I can see
which id to wait for without re-reading the child's description.

## Context

- `phase_drive()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 7934) loops
  over `phase_parent` reports and spawns a fresh Pi session per startable
  child. It already re-propagates `blocked_children` (ids only) on the
  "no startable child" path (~line 8368).
- After C2/C3 a child can be classified `skip-blocked` with `blocking_ids`;
  drive must not spawn a session for it and must surface the ids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No session is spawned for a child classified `skip-blocked` by the parent phase; `sessions_spawned` and `children_driven` reflect that (the child is not counted as driven, failed or retried).
- [ ] The drive report carries the blocked verdicts with their blocking ids — `blocked_children` keeps its existing id-list shape **and** the richer per-child entries (child id, status, `blocking_ids`, stale/unvalidated flags) are present, so both existing consumers (`tests/test_implement_drive.py::test_stops_when_no_startable_child`) and new ones work.
- [ ] The "no startable child" message names the blocking ids (not just "blocked or held"), so an unattended dispatcher log is actionable.
- [ ] Existing drive behaviour unchanged: per-child session bound, finish-attempt bound and reset-for-retry recovery, timeout reconciliation (`completed-late`), stranded-child detection, `skipped-held` propagation, recursion guard, and parent-advanced-last.
- [ ] C1 case (d) is green; the changed-scope suite (pytest + node where applicable) is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Reporting/loop-control change only — no new spawning policy, no change to
  `parent`'s classification (that is C2/C3) or to single-item `start`/`finish`.
- Do not weaken existing bounds or guards.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (~7934, report propagation ~8360-8380), `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `phase_parent` report fields from C2/C3.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — scripted-parent/recording-spawner harness; existing propagation test to extend.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — recovery behaviours that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1 case (d).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9` — drive: fresh session per child (the loop this extends).
- `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — `skipped-held` propagation precedent.

# Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2**, **C3** and **C4** (the vocabulary must match the shipped code).

## Goal

As an operator or agent reading the implement skill, I need the Guards list and
the parent-recursion section to state the blocked-child re-validation rule and
the new report vocabulary, so nobody re-learns it from a failed run.

## Context

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` "Guards (deterministic, in `phase_parent`)"
  currently says only: *"**Blocked children wait** — a child is only started
  once every in-chain blocker is terminal; otherwise it is reported in
  `blocked_children`."* and, earlier in the parent-recursion section, that
  cross-project blockers are "coordination notes" (the wording superseded by
  this work, originally from `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents report fields; extend it
  only where it already enumerates parent/drive report keys.
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py` enforce doc
  consistency — they must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary (`action: "skip-blocked"`, `blocking_ids`, `stale_blocks`, `unvalidated_blocks`, extended `blocked_children` entries). The rule is stated once: a child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block holds; the block is re-validated on every run against outbound dep edges and the explicit `Blocked by …` line.

# Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

**Headline:** `inject_refactor_comment()` unconditionally prepends its marker
block, so on any file that opens with `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (or a PEP 263
encoding line) the injected comment lands above the interpreter directive. The
resulting file is no longer directly executable and ruff reports `EXE005`
("Shebang should be at the beginning of the file") — a formatting finding filed
*against the file the skill just annotated*, which then spawns a fresh
low-priority refactor work item that only undoes the skill's own edit.

## Problem statement

`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` builds a marker block and writes
`new_content = comment_block + original_content`. For executable scripts this
breaks the shebang contract and creates a self-sustaining loop: the skill
injects a marker → the next refactor run's linter sees `EXE005` → a new work
item is filed → the fix deletes the marker → the next refactor run injects it
again.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement
  pipeline's refactor step — they inherit preventable lint findings and
  executable-bit regressions on files the skill touched.
- **Producers triaging the refactor backlog** — self-inflicted, duplicate items
  consume triage and implementation capacity.
- **Developers** — annotated scripts must stay directly runnable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inject_refactor_comment()` inserts its block *after* any shebang
      (`#!…`) and any PEP 263 coding line, and after a Python module docstring
      when the file opens with one; on files with none of these the block still
      goes to the top as today.
- [ ] Markdown/HTML block-style markers (`<!-- … -->`) keep their current
      placement behaviour, except that a leading shebang or coding line in a
      non-Markdown file is never displaced.
- [ ] Line endings and trailing newline state are preserved (write with
      `newline=""`), so the fix does not normalise CRLF files.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a file
      starting with a shebang, a file with shebang + coding line, a file with
      shebang + docstring, a plain Python file with no shebang, and a Markdown
      file — each asserting shebang stays on line 1.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that running the repository's lint gate over a
      file annotated by the skill reports no `EXE005`/`EXE001`-style executable
      findings.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (the "REFACTOR Comments"
      section), and any relevant docs entries.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change marker syntax, the duplicate-suppression match on smell
  type, or `get_comment_style()` file-type mapping — placement only.
- Removal of stale markers on work-item close is **out of scope**; that is
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`.
- Keep the change confined to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` and its
  tests.

## Existing state

```python
# skill/refactor/comment_injection.py
    # Place comment at the top of the file
    new_content = comment_block + original_content
```

`_build_comment_block()` prefixes the block with `"
"` unconditionally, so even
a token ending in a newline gains an extra blank line above the shebang.

Evidence from the field: on 2026-10-30 the implement pipeline's refactor step
annotated `src/rss_server.py` in the ContentCreator project, pushing
`#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1 to line 13 and producing
`EXE005 Shebang should be at the beginning of the file`. The finding was filed
as `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0`, implemented as removing the skill's own marker, and
pinned with `tests/test_rss_script_entrypoint.py`.

## Desired change

`inject_refactor_comment()` computes an insertion offset from the file head
(shebang, then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splices the
block there, leaving the file head byte-identical otherwise.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — compute insertion offset; write with
  `newline=""`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — placement tests for the
  shebang / coding-line / docstring / Markdown cases
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — state the placement rule in the "REFACTOR
  Comments" section

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a marker placed after the module docstring is still found by
  `has_existing_comment()`, which scans the whole file rather than the head.
- **Risk (low):** docstring detection is heuristic; an over-eager match could
  move the marker into the middle of code. Mitigation: match only a leading
  triple-quoted string that terminates before the first statement, and fall back
  to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "annotation lifecycle" refactor (placement,
  removal, sweep) is tempting. Record such work against
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` instead of widening this item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` — remove stale `REFACTOR-` markers when their work item
  closes (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — the ContentCreator item that this defect created
  (fixed by deleting the marker and pinning the entrypoint contract).
- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — the ContentCreator sweep of stale markers left in
  tests and scripts.
data.title: Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (or the equivalent hook page) — v2 wrapper
  contract

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.

# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` parses the Key Files section with
`stripped.startswith("**Key Files:**")` (`_parse_key_files_section`, ~line 147)
and the same literal test in `validate_key_files_format` (~line 243). A
description that writes the section as a markdown heading with a nested bold
marker — `## **Key Files:**` — never matches, so the plan skill's completeness
validation treats the section as absent and `validate_key_files_format` either
reports success on an empty list or warns "section is present but contains no
valid file paths" depending on the code path.

Consumers hit this: 9 of 386 items in the `tce-the-rising` store use
`## **Key Files:**` (the face-off tie epic RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight
children).

## Desired change

1. Accept the same forms as the fixed implement-skill parser
   (SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ): H1–H6 heading + `Key Files` with optional bold marker,
   optional parenthetical qualifier (`(predicted)`), optional closing `**`/`:`
   and case-insensitive matching; plus whitespace/colon-tolerant bare
   `**Key Files:**` lines.
2. Keep the existing behaviour of stopping the section at the next Markdown
   heading (SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2) and keep every currently accepted form working.

- `_parse_key_files_section` returns the listed paths for `## **Key Files:**`,

- **SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ** — the implement.py gate fix this follows.

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, I want the 2026-10-31 test-slot starvation fix proved shut with post-fix
measurements, and the remaining cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector removed, so that no agent
session loses minutes queueing for a 1–3 s test run and no two consumers pay twice for the same
full suite.

## Problem statement

The fast-lane fix (`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38` on 2026-10-31T23:21) delivered the
separate `test-fast` semaphore namespace, the re-derived `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 6` and
the `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` reporting. Two gaps remain from the original RCA item
(`LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`, llm repo — closed as superseded by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`):

1. **No post-fix measurement.** Its AC5 ("median blocked time per work item falls materially below
   ~10 min/test call; evidence recorded") was never executed. A preliminary scan of the 30 pi
   session logs touched since `a2659c38` found 12 `slot_wait_seconds` samples, all `0.00 s`, and
   zero `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notices — encouraging, but too small a sample to close
   the question, and it says nothing about the two dominant wait categories (`implement finish` and
   the dev-push full-suite gate), which appear as `wait_for_job` blocks, not `run_tests.py` JSON.
   The window is no longer thin: **2 439 session files post-date `a2659c38` and 4 044
   `slot_wait_seconds` occurrences are present** (planning-session scan, 2026-11-08), so a
   counted p50/p90/max per category is computable — the risk that remains is attribution, not
   volume.
2. **Verdicts are not reusable across consumers.** `run_cached()` keys on either the loose worktree
   fingerprint or — when the caller passes an explicit would-be-commit tree SHA — on
   `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. `implement.py` finish passes a tree SHA; the test CLI and the audit
   path pass nothing and keep historical loose-worktree keys. The dev-push gate (since
   `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH`) *is* bound to a subject — it passes `--gate-commit <local_sha>` and the
   runner resolves a clean checkout holding that commit — but it still keys the verdict on that
   checkout's **loose worktree state**, not on the pushed commit's **tree**. A green full-suite
   verdict recorded for tree *T* by a tree-keyed caller (the finish gate, or any future
   tree-keyed run) therefore cannot satisfy the gate for the same *T*, and the push re-executes
   the full suite.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs evidence, not anecdotes, that the critical starvation fix worked:
  *As the operator, I want a recorded p50/p90/max of post-fix slot wait so I can close the RCA with
  data rather than with the fix's assertion.*
- **Agent session** — *As an agent pushing to `dev`, I want the gate to reuse a green verdict for
  the tree I am pushing so my push does not cost a second 7–9 minute suite run.*

## Existing state (verified in source at planning time, 2026-11-08)

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: two lanes
  (`test`, `test-fast`), ceilings 6 and 4, `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane`/`slot_lanes` reported,
  `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notice at ≥ 1 s.
- `skill/test_cache.py`: `compute_tree_state(index_file)` → `git write-tree` SHA;
  `run_cached(..., fingerprint=<sha>)` keys lookup and store with
  `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`; `query_cached()` stays worktree-only by design.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: finish no longer runs a full suite at all — it defers to
  the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`) and passes the tree SHA for its changed-scope verdict
  (`SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`).
- `.githooks/pre-push` is **`worklog:pre-push-hook:v4`**, not v3, and it **already carries the
  pushed-commit guard** (`SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH`, `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B`): it forwards the pushed
  `<local_sha>` as `run_tests.py --gate-commit <sha>`; `resolve_gate_subject()` picks a checkout
  whose `HEAD` *is* that commit with no dirty paths (in place, else a clean `git worktree list`
  checkout) and **refuses** (exit 2, `run_tests: gate-refused …`) when none holds it. It emits
  `run_tests: gate-subject|gate-root|gate-verdict` provenance on stderr and mirrors the gate
  checkout's cache into the main checkout.
  **What is still missing:** `resolve_gate_subject()` computes no tree SHA,
  `GATE_SUBJECT_PREFIX` hard-codes `fingerprint_kind=worktree`, and `run_tests.py` exposes no CLI
  way to pass an explicit tree fingerprint — so the gate's verdict lives in the worktree-key
  namespace and cannot be shared with a tree-keyed caller.
- `.githooks/pre-push.v2` (installed into other projects) deliberately has no suite gate, so it
  needs no change.
- The `llm` repo is `~/projects/llm-manager` (its own wl store with `LP-` ids, its own
  `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`). Its hook is a **v4 variant with its own inline pushed-commit guard**
  (compares `local_sha` with the gate tree's `HEAD` and requires a clean tree) and runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root <root>` — it does **not** use
  `--gate-commit`, has no gate-reason classifier, and keys on worktree state. It needs a `git pull`
  before any follow-up work there (producer, planning session).

## Desired change

1. Re-measure the post-fix wait distribution with a reproducible, read-only analysis and record it
   (method + numbers) in this item.
2. Key the pre-push gate's verdict on the pushed commit's **tree** (plumbed through the runner
   CLI), keeping the existing pushed-commit guard as a regression constraint, so the verdict lands
   in the same namespace as the finish gate's and is reused when the tree matches; report cache
   hit/miss and entry age so a served verdict is visible.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Post-fix re-measurement recorded.** A reproducible read-only analysis (committed script, cited
   in this item with the exact command) over every pi session log covering at least 24 h after
   `a2659c38` (or all sessions since 2026-10-31T23:21 if fewer) reports, per wait category —
   (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait, split by lane (`test` = full, `test-fast` = partial),
   (b) `implement finish`, (c) dev-push full-suite gate — the call count and p50/p90/max wall
   clock, with the sample count stated next to every percentile.
   Pass: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`, partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no
   `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded honestly and filed as follow-up work, not
   smoothed over.
2. **The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree.** The gate derives the pushed commit's tree SHA
   (`git rev-parse <local_sha>^{tree}`) and passes it explicitly, so the verdict is stored and
   looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. The existing pushed-commit guard
   (`--gate-commit` clean-checkout resolution, shipped `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH`) is preserved
   unchanged as a regression constraint — this AC re-scopes the earlier "add the guard" wording,
   which the source shows is already delivered. When the guard fails or the tree SHA cannot be
   computed the gate refuses rather than falling back to a loose worktree key (fail-closed,
   matching the cache's provenance contract), with a loud refusal naming the commit, the resolved
   HEAD, the tree path, the recovery step and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
3. **Cross-consumer reuse proven.** A test demonstrates that a full-suite verdict recorded for tree
   *T* by one caller (finish gate / tree-keyed `run_cached`) is served as a cache hit to the
   pre-push gate for the same *T*, and that a different tree *T′* misses. The gate reports cache
   hit/miss (and the reused entry's age) in its stderr/JSON output so a served verdict is visible.
4. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`),
   rejected (exit 2) when the value is not a usable tree SHA or the mode cannot bind it, and
   documented in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`. The pre-push contract in the same document
   (§0.3 "Explicit-fingerprint override", §0.4 "Pre-push gate subject binding") and the hook's
   header comment are updated: the gate's key is the pushed **tree**, not the resolved checkout's
   loose worktree state. (`docs/dev/git-hooks.md` does not exist in this repository — the
   pre-push contract lives in `test-skill-reference.md` and the hook header; the stale reference is
   corrected rather than a new document invented.)
5. **Tests.** Deterministic tests cover: the gate computes and passes the pushed tree SHA; a
   same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss; fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`,
   when the tree is dirty, or when the tree SHA is unavailable; worktree-keyed callers' cache keys
   are unchanged byte for byte. Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests
   stay green. Test homes: `tests/test_pre_push_gate_subject.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
   `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs`, `skill/test/tests/`.
6. **Rollout is explicit, not implicit.** The item records that `pre-push.v2` consumers are
   unaffected (no suite gate) and that the `llm` repo (`~/projects/llm-manager`, diverged v4 hook
   with an inline guard keyed on worktree state) needs its own change, tracked as a follow-up item
   in that repository's own wl store (created after a `git pull` — local store is at schema v8,
   application expects v9).
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository scope:** implementation lands in this repo only (`skill/test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, docs,
  tests). The `llm` repo's v4 hook is a follow-up in that repo; `ContextHub` and others receive
  `pre-push.v2` (no suite gate) and need nothing.
- **No synthetic saturation.** Measurement must be read-only log analysis; the host is live and a
  synthetic burst would manufacture the very contention being measured (same deliberate scope
  decision as `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`).
- **Cache correctness first.** Never degrade to a state-independent fallback key and never serve a
  tree verdict for a different tree; an unfingerprintable run simply executes fresh.
- **POSIX `sh` hook.** No new dependency, no `bash`-isms in `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Test execution policy.** All test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); no ad-hoc
  `pytest` invocations.
- **Do not edit the pacer/lane semantics** delivered by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — this item only
  measures them and changes cache keying.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI flag for an explicit tree fingerprint, threaded to
  `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`; `resolve_gate_subject()` gains the pushed commit's tree SHA
  and `_emit_gate_subject()`/`_emit_gate_verdict()` report the tree key, hit/miss and entry age.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — only if a committed-state tree helper is needed (likely not: the gate
  uses `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`, no index file), plus the existing `fingerprint_kind` plumbing.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — pass the tree fingerprint through the runner CLI, echo hit/miss, keep the
  guard and the POSIX `sh` constraint.
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_subject.py` — tree-keying, hit/miss and refusal cases (existing home).
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — same-tree hit / different-tree miss / byte-identical worktree keys.
- `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` — hook-level assertions (flag presence, refusal paths,
  hit/miss echo).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` — tree-kind entry used as the
  cross-consumer reuse source.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — flag documentation and the corrected gate-subject contract.
- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — the read-only measurement script (pattern:
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`), over pi session logs under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — mis-attribution in the measurement.** Waits for `implement finish` and the dev-push gate
  surface as `wait_for_job` blocks rather than `run_tests.py` JSON, so a naive grep can double-count
  or miss them. *Mitigation:* F1 classifies by call site and unit-tests the parser against synthetic
  fixtures; the report states counts next to every percentile and names the window.
- **Risk — cache poisoning by a wrong tree key.** A bug here could serve a green verdict for an
  untested tree. *Mitigation:* fail closed, plus explicit same-tree/different-tree tests and reuse of
  the already-audited `fingerprint_kind` machinery.
- **Risk — hook divergence drift.** Per-repo copies (`llm-manager` v4 variant, `pre-push.v2`) mean
  the fix can land in `SorraAgents` yet not reach a project. *Mitigation:* AC6 + a follow-up item in
  the llm store.
- **Risk — scope creep into the wider RCA amplifiers** (`drive` nested waits, finish lock
  serialisation, agents raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to 5400 s). Recorded as linked follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption —** the dominant residual cost is the dev-push gate suite, not finish, because finish
  no longer runs a full suite (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`). The AC1 measurement either confirms or
  refutes this, and refutation re-opens the amplifier list rather than silently narrowing the item.
- **Assumption —** the gate keeps resolving a clean checkout of the pushed commit even when a
  tree-kind verdict already exists. Serving a tree hit with *no* clean checkout available is a
  behaviour change to the shipped guard and is deliberately out of scope (fail-closed wins).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — fast lane + calibrated ceiling + `slot_wait` reporting (**shipped
  `a2659c38`**); supersedes AC1–AC3 of the original RCA.
- `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM` (llm store) — the original RCA item; closed as superseded, its AC4 residual
  and AC5 re-measurement are this item's scope.
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push gate (makes AC4 of the old
  item largely obsolete and creates the reuse gap addressed here).
- `SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB` / `SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD` — tree-bound finish verdicts and their documented
  contract (the precedent this item extends to the pre-push gate).
- `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH` — pre-push gate bound to the pushed commit (the shipped guard AC2 preserves);
  its discovery record is `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B`.
- `SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D` — runner duration/timeout/kill/slot-wait facts (source of
  `slot_wait_seconds`).
- Open amplifiers, already tracked: `SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` (a low-ceiling waiter never probes
  higher-numbered free slots), `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (dev pushes starve/flake under load),
  `SA-0MVEEALZR0029DD7` (single-flight coalescing of identical in-flight suite runs).
- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — finish gate: classify timeouts/kills and report slot queue wait separately.
- `LP-0MW7C8QIQ0028O2M` (llm-manager store) — **follow-up created 2026-11-08**: adopt the
  tree-keyed gate subject, `--gate-commit`, provenance echo and gate-reason classifier in that
  repository's hook (pull first; store at schema v8).
- Pushed-commit-guard precedents: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` (llm v4 hook guard, in the
  `~/projects/llm-manager` store), `LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT` (llm: gate validated the main checkout, not
  the pushed commit — completed). Cross-store ids are not resolvable from this repo's `wl`.
- Adjacent, open, *not* in scope: `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` / `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` (implement.py must
  push from the tree it is pushing) — they concern which tree `finish` pushes, not the hook's own
  fingerprint.

## Plan (5 features, test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------|
| F1 | Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (`SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K`) | task | — | AC1 |
| F2 | Reproduce same-tree duplicate suite (`SA-0MW7C6A9R000PD98`) | task | — | AC3, AC7 |
| F3 | Runner CLI tree-fingerprint surface (`SA-0MW7C6AYO0062GJB`) | feature | — | AC4, AC5, AC8 |
| F4 | Gate keys on the pushed tree (`SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG`) | feature | F2, F3 | AC2, AC3, AC5, AC7 |
| F5 | Gate contract docs and rollout record (`SA-0MW7C6CB3007BODF`) | docs | F1, F4 | AC4, AC6, AC8 |

Six automated review stages ran on this plan (requirements/AC alignment, completeness incl. `**Key
Files:**` validation, sequencing/dependencies, scope sizing, acceptance/testability, polish/handoff);
the AC coverage review reports **100 %** (9/9 parent ACs covered, no gaps, no conflicts).

Phasing is vertical: F1 delivers script + tests + recorded numbers; F2 delivers a hermetic
regression test (the test-first item) that F4 flips; F3/F4 each deliver code + tests + docs in the
same slice; F5 closes the contract and rollout record. Between phases, review the next child's
description against what landed (F2's baseline assertion must be flipped by F4, not deleted).

Design note for F4: the tree SHA is derived **inside the runner** where `--gate-commit` is already
resolved (`git rev-parse <local_sha>^{tree}` → `fingerprint`), so the POSIX `sh` hook needs no new
git call and keeps echoing the `run_tests: gate-*` lines; if the hook must pass the tree
explicitly instead, it does so with `git rev-parse "$sha^{tree}"` and fails closed on an empty
result.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-08 — `/skill:plan` decomposition; description corrected against source (hook is v4 with a
  shipped pushed-commit guard; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` absent here; measurement window large; llm
  repo is `~/projects/llm-manager`); AC2/AC4/AC6 re-scoped per producer answers Q4/Q5; five children
  created (F1–F5) with test-first dependency edges; coverage review 9/9.

## Impact

An agent pushing to `dev` no longer pays twice for the same full suite — a green verdict for the
tree it is pushing is reused — and the operator can close the slot-starvation RCA on counted
p50/p90/max evidence instead of on the fix's own assertion.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (producer, interactive reply):** "`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` already holds AC1–AC3; what should
  happen to `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`?" — Options: (a) close as superseded and file the residual here,
  (b) narrow the `llm` item and implement cross-repo, (c) close as fully superseded and drop
  AC4/AC5.
  **Answer: "1. A"** — close the `llm` item as superseded; the residual (AC4 gap + AC5
  re-measurement) is filed as this item. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  verified `a2659c38` in `SorraAgents` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT == 6`, `test-fast` lane,
  live `slot_lane=fast`, `slot_wait=0.00007s`); verified none of the named files exist in the `llm`
  checkout, so an `llm`-store item could not satisfy worktree isolation.
- **Q2 (producer, interactive reply):** "Residual scope?" — Options: (a) re-measure only,
  (b) re-measure + tree-keyed pre-push gate, (c) re-measure + the wider amplifiers from the RCA.
  **Answer: "2. b"**; producer also asked for follow-up work to be recommended and offered as new
  work items rather than silently folded in. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" documents that the pre-push
  gate keys on loose worktree state; `run_cached`/`run_suite` already accept an explicit tree
  fingerprint, so the change is a CLI + hook plumbing problem, not a cache redesign.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection, no producer input needed):** "Does `implement finish` still run
  a full suite whose verdict the pre-push gate could reuse?" — **Answer: no**; finish defers the
  full suite to the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`, `fe85415a`, 2026-10-19), which is why the
  old AC4 is re-scoped to cross-consumer keying rather than finish→pre-push handoff. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` step 3b comment.
- **Q4 (planning session, producer, interactive reply):** "AC2 as written says the gate 'first adds
  the pushed-commit guard this hook currently lacks', but `.githooks/pre-push` is v4 and already
  passes `--gate-commit <local_sha>` (clean-checkout resolution + refusal, `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH`).
  Re-scope AC2?" — Options: (a) re-scope to the tree-keying increment, keeping the guard and
  fail-closed behaviour as regression constraints, (b) keep AC2 as written and re-implement the
  guard, (c) drop all guard reference and keep only tree keying.
  **Answer: "4. A"** — re-scope to tree keying; the guard stays as a regression constraint.
  Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-08. Research: read `.githooks/pre-push` (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v4`,
  header note 4a, `resolve_gate_subject()`), `run_tests.py` (`GATE_SUBJECT_PREFIX` hard-codes
  `fingerprint_kind=worktree`), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3–0.4.
- **Q5 (planning session, producer, interactive reply):** "AC6 requires a follow-up item for the
  `llm` repo's v4 hook, but the `llm` checkout appeared absent (`~/projects/llm/` holds only an empty
  `slot-cache/`; `wl show LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` → not found from this repo). Where should the
  follow-up live?" — Options: (a) create it in this store tagged `cross-repo`, (b) record the
  rollout fact in this item only, (c) drop the `llm`-hook note as obsolete.
  **Answer: "5. The LLM does exist locally, it is in ../llm-manager, it will need a git pull"** —
  i.e. the llm repo is `~/projects/llm-manager` with its own wl store, and the follow-up belongs
  there (pull first). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-08. Research: verified
  `~/projects/llm-manager` is a git checkout on `dev` whose `.worklog` store answers `LP-` ids

## Summary

`implement.py start` derives the canonical worktree path **and** branch name from the work item's *current* title slug (`worktree_path_for()` / `branch_name_for()`). If the title is edited after the worktree was created, `start` computes a different path and branch, so:

- the resume check (`_is_worktree(abs_wt_path)`) misses the existing worktree, and
- `git worktree add -b <new-branch> .worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<new-slug> dev` **succeeds**, silently creating a second, empty worktree for the same item while the real in-progress work stays in the old one.

`phase_start` never consults `_discover_worktree()` (which does scan `.worklog/worktrees/`), unlike `finish`/`abort`/`parent`.

## Why it matters

A driven child (or any resumed session) can then implement into the wrong tree or lose track of prior work; `finish` may remove the emptier tree while the real work is stranded. Title edits are a normal operator action (clarifying scope during planning).

## Expected behaviour

`start` should resume the item's **existing** worktree (and its existing branch) even when the current title slug differs from the directory/branch name created at start time. A second worktree must never be created for an item that already has one.

## Suggested approach

- Before computing a fresh path, consult the existing-discovery mechanism (`_discover_worktree`, or a `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*/` scan that checks `.implement_state.json` / registered worktree branches for the item id) and reuse the found path and its checked-out branch.
- Fall back to the current path/slug computation only when no worktree exists for the item.
- Add a regression test: real git repo + worktree created for slug A, then `wl` title changed to slug B, then `start` from the main checkout (and from inside the worktree) — assert one worktree only, no new branch, and the report names the existing path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** After the work item title changes, `start` resumes the existing worktree and branch for the item instead of creating a second worktree/branch.
- **AC2:** `start` run from inside the existing (old-slug) worktree resumes it after a title change.
- **AC3:** When no worktree exists for the item, behaviour is unchanged (fresh path/branch from the current title slug).
- **AC4:** Regression tests cover AC1–AC3 with a real temporary git repo plus linked worktree.
- **AC5:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related work

- Discovered while scoping `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF` (resume from inside a linked worktree); discovery report `AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY`.
- Out of scope for that fix: it only corrects the *base* against which the default path is resolved.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()`, `_discover_worktree()`, `worktree_path_for()`, `branch_name_for()`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_worktree_resume.py` (or a new slug-drift test module) — real git fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — resume semantics wording.

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm).
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`, `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (ground truth).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. Without clone detection, redundancy grows unnoticed because nothing forces a re-examination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detects near-duplicate test blocks (within and across files) using normalised AST/token similarity, not raw text matching.
- [ ] Reports clusters with file, line range and similarity score, ordered by redundancy.
- [ ] Distinguishes legitimate repetition (table-driven cases, parameterised variants) from redundant duplication, and defaults to reporting rather than removal.
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with thresholds and limitations documented.
- [ ] Performance is bounded on a large suite (documented sampling/scope options).
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Read-only; no automatic deletion.
- Conservative thresholds; a false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a miss.
- No hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (additive accumulation is its stated failure mode).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; this analyser is a complementary cheap signal.
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
