# Document no-op finish + full-suite verify

## Context

Parent SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1. The prior slices change finish's contract: a
clean, commit-less worktree is no longer finalised by default, and the
verification-only path is opt-in. Agents must know this before they meet it,
and the implement-skill references must describe the refusal instead of
presenting the no-op path as an unconditional success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC6 — Documentation: `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (and any related implement-skill docs) documents the new no-op semantics, the `--verification-only` flag (including `start --verification-only` recording the signal in the worktree state), and how the agent should treat a clean, commit-less worktree.
- AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC8 — The full project test suite passes with the new changes (test skill, full scope; any failure triaged into a critical `test-failure` item).

## Minimal implementation

- Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (§ Terminal status on both finish paths and the finish step list) to describe the refusal, the opt-in flag, and the work-less worktree guidance (re-enter the worktree and produce work, or use the flag for verification-only items).
- Update `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`'s terminal-status read-back section with the new no-op refusal contract and the classification verdict.
- Refresh the affected code comments/docstrings (`git_commit`, `_assert_terminal_status`, `_classify_child`) and any README pointer to the implement skill contract.
- Run the full suite via the test skill and record the verdict.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish contract, flag documentation, work-less worktree guidance.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — terminal-status read-back and no-op refusal reference.
- `README.md` — any implement-skill contract pointer that needs the new semantics.

## Definition of done

- Docs state the default refusal, the `--verification-only` opt-in, and the not-finalisable classification.
- Full-suite verdict green (or failures triaged).

## Impact

Agents and operators learn the new finish contract from the docs before they
hit a refusal, so a commit-less worktree is treated as unfinished work rather
than a silent completion.

Parent: **SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV** (test-slot contention: re-measure post-fix wait, tree-key the
pre-push gate). Covers parent AC1.

## Target outcome

Prove — or refute — with counted data that the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix
(`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38`) removed test-slot starvation, using a committed
read-only analysis over the pi session logs rather than an anecdote or a synthetic load test.
Baseline established at planning time (2026-11-08): 2 439 session files post-date `a2659c38` and
4 044 `slot_wait_seconds` occurrences exist, so the sample is large; what must be earned is
**attribution** of the waits to the three call sites.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` exists, is read-only (pattern:
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`), and emits a deterministic JSON report.
- Unit tests cover the parser with synthetic log fixtures (no live session store, no test runs).
- The measured numbers, the exact command and the window are recorded as a comment on
  `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV`.
- Pass/fail is evaluated honestly against the parent's thresholds; a miss becomes a linked
  follow-up item, never a footnote.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-fix re-measurement recorded: a committed read-only script `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`
   (`--since`, `--sessions-root`, `--json`) analyses every pi session log under the sessions root
   and reports, per wait category, the call count and p50/p90/max wall clock for
   (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait from `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` (split by lane: `test` = full,
   `test-fast` = partial), (b) `implement finish` wait, (c) dev-push full-suite gate wait.
2. The measurement covers at least 24 h after `a2659c38` (2026-10-31T23:21) — or every session
   since that timestamp if fewer — and the report states the window start/end, the number of
   session files scanned and the sample count next to every percentile.
3. Pass/fail is evaluated on the parent's thresholds: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`,
   partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded
   honestly and filed as a follow-up work item, not smoothed over.
4. The numbers and the exact command that produced them are recorded as a comment on
   `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV`; a category with too few samples is labelled "no regression observed in
   N samples" with a re-check date rather than quoted as a percentile.
5. Parser tests (executed through the test skill) cover synthetic fixtures: escaped JSON-in-JSON
   tool output, missing keys, lane attribution, and double-count avoidance. No test reads the live
   session store or runs a suite.
6. The script never runs a test, never acquires a semaphore slot and never writes to the session
   store — read-only log analysis, no synthetic saturation (parent constraint).

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — the analysis script (new).
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — parser/fixture tests (new home; keep it under `tests/` so the
  pytest suite picks it up).
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — the pattern for a read-only analysis script.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — a short method note so the re-check can be re-run without
  re-deriving the classification rules.

## Deliverables

- Read-only measurement script + fixture tests.
- Recorded p50/p90/max per category (with counts, window and command) as a comment on the parent.
- Follow-up items for any threshold miss.

## Dependencies

- None. Safe to run first: it touches no production code path.

Parent: **SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV**. **Test-first item** for F3/F4 — it pins the defect before the fix.
Covers parent AC3 and AC7.

## Target outcome

Capture, hermetically, the current cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector as an executable baseline:
a green full-suite verdict recorded for tree *T* by a tree-keyed caller (the finish gate's
`run_cached(..., fingerprint=T)` path) is **not** served to the pre-push gate for the same *T*, so
the push pays for the suite twice. The fix (F4) flips this assertion to a hit.

## Definition of done

- A hermetic test in `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` builds a temp git repo, records a
  full-scope tree-kind verdict for *T* through the tree-keyed cache path, and asserts today's
  behaviour (miss) with the defect documented inline.
- The post-fix expectation is written into the test (a hit for *T*, a miss for a different *T′*)
  so F4 flips an assertion instead of adding new, unfocused coverage.
- The test completes in seconds and needs no real worklog, network, session store or test slot.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Cross-consumer baseline captured: a hermetic test records a full-suite verdict for tree *T*
   through the tree-keyed `run_cached(..., fingerprint=T)` path and asserts that the pre-push
   gate's lookup for the same tree *T* is a **cache miss** on today's code, with the duplicate-suite
   vector and this item's id documented inline above the assertion.
2. The assertion records the post-fix expectation — a cache **hit** for the same tree *T* and a
   **miss** for a different tree *T′* — as a documented expected-behaviour comment that F4 turns
   into the live assertion; the test must not be deleted or weakened when it is flipped.
3. The fixture is hermetic: temp git repository, no real worklog, no network, no live session
   store, no test-slot acquisition, and the test completes in under 5 seconds.
4. The test is executed through the test skill and is green on landing (the baseline assertion is
   about today's behaviour, not a committed red test).
5. A same-tree hit is demonstrated at the cache layer in the same fixture (so the baseline failure
   is attributable to the gate's key, not to a broken cache write).

## Key Files

- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` — new fixture + baseline assertion.
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_subject.py` — the existing gate-subject harness style to follow.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the gate lookup path under test (`resolve_gate_subject`,
  `run_all(fingerprint=…)`).
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached(..., fingerprint=…)` used to record the tree-kind verdict.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — cache fixtures/helpers that can be reused.

## Deliverables

- Failing-baseline-style regression test (green on landing, flipped by F4).
- Inline documented capture of the duplicate-suite vector.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first). F4 depends on this item.

Parent: **SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV**. Covers parent AC4, AC5 (runner side) and AC8.

## Target outcome

Give `run_tests.py` a first-class way to bind a full-suite run to an explicit would-be-commit tree
SHA, so every consumer — the pre-push gate now (F4), and any future tree-keyed caller — can store
and look up a verdict in the `fingerprint_kind="tree"` namespace. `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`
already thread the parameter; what is missing is the CLI surface, its fail-closed validation and its
documented contract.

## Definition of done

- `run_tests.py --fingerprint <sha>` binds a `--scope full` run to that tree, storing and looking up
  the entry with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.
- Invalid combinations and unusable values are rejected with exit 2 and an actionable message —
  never a silent fallback to a loose worktree key.
- Callers that pass nothing keep byte-identical worktree keys (asserted, not merely implied).
- The flag and its contract are documented; no pacer/lane semantics change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`),
   rejected (exit 2) when the value is unusable or the mode cannot bind it, and documented in
   `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`; the same document's pre-push contract and the hook's header
   comment are updated by the final docs item (SA-0MW7C6CB3007BODF) so the gate's key is the pushed
   tree rather than the resolved checkout's worktree state.
2. Fail-closed validation: the flag is rejected (exit 2, actionable message) when the value is not a
   usable tree SHA or when combined with a mode it cannot bind (`--scope changed`), instead of
   silently falling back to a loose worktree key.
3. Deterministic tests cover: store plus immediate hit for the same fingerprint; miss for a
   different fingerprint; a legacy/foreign worktree entry missing a tree request; and both
   rejection paths.
4. Worktree-keyed callers' cache keys are unchanged byte for byte — asserted explicitly in
   `tests/test_test_cache.py` rather than only implied by existing tests — and existing
   cache/provenance tests stay green.
5. No pacer/lane semantics change: `slot_lane`/`slot_wait_seconds` reporting and the `test` (ceiling
   6) / `test-fast` (ceiling 4) lanes are untouched and their regression tests stay green.
6. The docstring, `--help` text and the reference doc describe the flag as fail-closed: an
   unfingerprintable run executes fresh, a tree entry never satisfies a worktree request (and vice
   versa), and the stored entry is recorded with `fingerprint_kind="tree"` for a supplied value.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `build_parser()`, the `--scope full` dispatch, the
  `fingerprint` threading into `run_all`/`run_suite`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — CLI behaviour home for scope/fingerprint tests.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — cache-key determinism and byte-identical worktree-key assertions.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — § "Explicit-fingerprint override" and the CLI reference.

## Deliverables

- Explicit regression assertion that unfingerprinted callers keep their historical keys.

data.description:
Parent: **SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV**. Covers parent AC2, AC3, AC5 and AC7. Depends on **F2** (test-first
baseline) and **F3** (CLI surface).

## Target outcome

Make the dev-push full-suite gate's verdict a statement about the pushed commit's **tree**, not
about whichever checkout it happened to measure, so a green verdict is reusable by any tree-keyed
consumer and a repeated push for the same tree costs seconds instead of a second 7–9 minute suite.
The pushed-commit guard shipped by `SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH` (`--gate-commit` → a clean checkout of
exactly that commit, else refuse) is preserved unchanged as a regression constraint; what changes is
the cache key and its reporting.

## Definition of done

- The gate derives `git rev-parse <local_sha>^{tree}` and passes it as the explicit tree
  fingerprint; verdicts land in `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.
- A verdict recorded for tree *T* by another tree-keyed caller is served as a hit for the same *T*;
  a different tree misses.
- hit/miss and the reused entry's age are reported in the `run_tests: gate-*` provenance lines the
  hook already echoes.
- Every refusal path fails closed with an actionable message; no path falls back to a worktree key.
- F2's baseline assertion is flipped to expect the hit, and the full pre-push/gate test set stays
  green.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree: the pushed commit's tree SHA
   (`git rev-parse <local_sha>^{tree}`) is derived and passed explicitly, so the verdict is stored
   and looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"` — the same namespace as the finish gate's tree
   verdicts. The existing pushed-commit guard (`resolve_gate_subject()`: in-place checkout, else a
   clean `git worktree list` checkout, else refuse) is preserved unchanged as a regression
   constraint.
2. Cross-consumer reuse proven: a full-suite verdict recorded for tree *T* by a tree-keyed caller
   (finish gate / `run_cached(fingerprint=T)`) is served as a cache hit to the pre-push gate for the
   same *T*, and a different tree *T′* misses — F2's baseline assertion flipped, not deleted.
3. The gate reports cache hit/miss and the reused entry's age (`cache_hit`, `cache_age_seconds`)
   together with `fingerprint_kind=tree` in its stderr provenance (`run_tests: gate-verdict …`) and
   in its JSON output, and `.githooks/pre-push` echoes those lines to the pusher so a served verdict
   is visible.
4. Fail-closed refusal: the gate refuses (non-zero exit, nothing executed) when the pushed-commit
   guard fails (`HEAD != local_sha`, dirty tree) or when the tree SHA cannot be computed, naming the
   commit, the resolved HEAD, the tree path, the recovery step and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` — it never
   falls back to a loose worktree key (matching the cache's provenance contract).
5. The gate's cache mirroring still works for tree-kind entries: the entry the gate wrote or reused
   is present in the main checkout's cache so post-push verification and the audit path can read it.
6. Deterministic tests (hermetic, executed through the test skill) cover: the gate computes and
   passes the pushed tree SHA; a same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss;
   fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`, when the tree is dirty, and when the tree SHA is
   unavailable; plus hook-level assertions in `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` (guard and echo
   behaviour). Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests stay green.
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
9. The POSIX `sh` hook constraint is respected: no new dependency and no `bash`-isms. Preferred
   design: the runner derives the tree where `--gate-commit` is already resolved, so the hook needs
   no new git call; if the hook passes the tree explicitly instead, it uses
   `git rev-parse "$sha^{tree}"` and fails closed on an empty result.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `resolve_gate_subject()` (add the tree SHA to the evidence),
  `_emit_gate_subject()`, `_emit_gate_verdict()` (hit/miss/age), the `--gate-commit` dispatch.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — lookup result must expose the reused entry's age for reporting.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — echo the extended provenance; keep the guard and POSIX `sh`.
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_subject.py` — tree-keying and refusal cases (existing home).
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` — F2's flipped assertion.
- `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` — hook-level assertions.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` — tree-kind verdict used as the reuse
  source.

## Deliverables

- Tree-keyed pre-push gate with hit/miss/age reporting.
- Flipped cross-consumer reuse proof plus the full refusal matrix.
- Evidence that the shipped pushed-commit guard is unchanged (regression tests).

## Dependencies

- **F2** — the baseline assertion this item flips.
- **F3** — the explicit tree-fingerprint CLI surface.

discovered-from:SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR

## Problem

`implement.py drive --pane-sessions` cannot drive a real (multi-minute) child
session. `_pane_session_spawner` calls
`HerdrSessionClient.prompt_agent(..., timeout_ms=child_timeout * 1000)`, but
the client is constructed with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60.0` and `_invoke()` passes
that value as `subprocess.run(timeout=...)`. The herdr CLI's own `--timeout`
argument is therefore irrelevant: the client kills the
`herdr agent prompt --wait` subprocess after 60 seconds and the spawner
reports `Pane agent for <child> did not complete: herdr call timed out`.

Observed during SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR: the driven child's pane was closed and its
session killed after ~70 s, with the child still `in-progress` and an empty
worktree, so the drive chain stopped on its first child and had to fall back
to the headless transport.

## Desired change

Scale the client's per-call subprocess timeout to the wait it is performing
(e.g. build the pane spawner's client with `timeout=child_budget + slack`, or
add a per-call timeout override to `_invoke`), so a pane-driven child session
can run for its whole documented budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A pane-driven child session whose turn takes longer than 60 s is not
  killed by the client; the recorded failure is the CLI's own `--timeout`
  verdict, never `herdr call timed out`.
- AC2: A unit test drives `_pane_session_spawner` with a slow fake herdr
  runner and asserts the client's subprocess timeout exceeds the requested
  child budget.
- AC3: The headless transport is unchanged.

## Notes

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR; that item fell back to the
headless spawner (`--no-pane-sessions`) to avoid the 60 s kill.
data.title: Pane-session drive always kills child sessions at 60s: HerdrSessionClient subprocess timeout is not the child budget

## Summary

Refactor duplicate prevention is a **substring match over other items' titles and descriptions**, keyed on file + line + rule code. It silently fails whenever the line number moves by one, whenever the path prefix differs (worktree vs main checkout), or whenever the title has been truncated — so the same smell is re-filed on every scan.

## Evidence

Function: `_has_existing_worklog_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`. It lists `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, concatenates each item's title and description, and returns a match only when **all three** of `target_file`, `target_code` and `str(target_line)` appear anywhere in that blob.

Open-backlog duplicates measured on 2026-11-08:

| Target | Rule | Open items for the same file+rule |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` | `S112` | 22 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` | `SIM117` | 10 |
| `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` | `ISC004` | 7 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py` | `SIM117` | 4 |
| `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` | `RUF015` | 4 |

Failure modes that defeat the guard:

1. **Line drift** — inserting one line above a finding changes every subsequent line number, so `str(target_line) in combined` no longer matches.
2. **Path-prefix drift** — the identical file is recorded as `/repo/.worklog/worktrees/wl-…/skill/x.py` from one scan and `/repo/skill/x.py` from another; neither is a substring of the other.
3. **Truncation** — titles are truncated in listing output (e.g. `[MEDIUM] /home/…/test_implement_push_fro`), so the full path is not present to match on.
4. **Cross-family blindness** — the guard only inspects `Refactor`-tagged items, so the audit-side family `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (73 open items, created by `audit_runner.py`) is invisible to it and mints parallel twins for the same diagnostics.

Note also that a substring match on a *line number* is not an identity: `str(12)` matches `:12`, `:120`, `:312`, and any mention of 12 anywhere in a long description.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Identity for a refactor finding is `(repository-relative path, rule/smell code)` — **not** the line number, and not the absolute path. The content fingerprint required by the re-verification item (`SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`) is stored alongside it so occurrences can be counted rather than guessed at.
2. Before creating an item the skill queries the existing open items for that exact identity **and** for the audit-created `ruff <RULE> in <path>` family, so the two producers cannot mint twins.
3. A repeat finding on an existing identity does not create a new item: it appends a comment recording the new line numbers/occurrences, or updates the existing item, per a documented rule.
4. Worktree path prefixes are normalised before comparison (shared helper, reused by the critical bug on worktree-path recording).
5. Line-level reporting is preserved: the item lists every affected line, so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail.
6. Regression tests covering: same smell twice in one run; smell re-found after a line shift; same file scanned from two worktrees; two different rules in one file; refactor-created vs audit-created twin suppression.
7. A one-off consolidation of the existing duplicates is possible from the same helper (dry-run first), so the backlog can be collapsed without manual wl calls.

## Related

- Critical bug `SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2`: refactor filings record ephemeral implement-worktree paths (the path-drift half of this problem; the shared path-normalisation helper is specified there and reused here).
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`: linter-derived items are never re-verified — supplies the content fingerprint and the occurrence re-check.
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS`: children survive parent deletion — the orphan half of the same backlog-hygiene gap.

## Impact

The same code smell is tracked once instead of up to twenty-two times, so the backlog reflects genuine debt and agents stop re-fixing work that is already queued.
data.title: Refactor dedupe (_has_existing_worklog_item) matches substrings of line/path, so the same smell is filed repeatedly

data.description:
## Summary

Nothing ever re-checks a linter-derived work item against the current tree. Once filed, a refactor or audit finding stays open until a human or agent happens to look at it — even when the target file has been deleted or the diagnostic has not fired for weeks.

During the 2026-11-08 backlog review this was measured directly, and every sampled family was stale.

## Evidence

**115 open refactor items whose titled path no longer resolves or whose diagnostic no longer reproduces:**

| Class | Items | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Target file deleted from the repo (`skill/proxy-usage-analysis/**`, a removed skill) | 37 | path does not exist |
| Target file exists, diagnostic no longer fires | 78 | `ruff check --isolated --select <RULE> <path>` → 0 hits in all 34 (path, rule) groups |

**73 open audit-side items** of the form `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (`audit_runner.py` `FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION`, created as "producer decision required" chores): **0 of 19 (path, rule) groups still fire** on the current tree.

Concrete examples of no-longer-reproducing findings that remained open:
- `S112` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — 22 items, 0 hits now.
- `SIM117` in `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — 10 items, 0 hits now.
- `ISC004` in `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — 7 items, 0 hits now.
- `PYI034`/`PYI036` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — 4 items, 0 hits now (these were orphaned children too).

Some of these block audits rather than sitting idle, so stale findings are not merely noise: `SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42` records the audit-side variant where every medium/low candidate-false-positive chore sets `needsProducerReview` and blocks closure.

## Why it matters

Stale items are indistinguishable from live work in every view. `wl next` will dispatch them, an agent will implement, and the audit skill must then decide whether a finding that no longer reproduces has been "fixed". The backlog reads as 444 actionable items when a large share are already resolved.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Every linter-derived item records, at creation, the **exact verification command** and a **content fingerprint** (file hash + rule set) that produced it.
2. A re-verification sweep re-runs that command and, per item, classifies it as `still-reproduces`, `no-longer-reproduces` or `target-gone`, recording the evidence in a comment.
3. Items classified `target-gone` are closed with a rationale (or flagged for deletion), and items classified `no-longer-reproduces` are closed with the evidence comment — **never silently**.
4. The sweep is **dry-run by default** and only ever touches items it can attribute to a linter family (`Refactor` tag, `[SEVERITY] <path>` titles, `ruff <RULE> in <path>` titles). It must never close a human-authored bug or feature.
5. The sweep is runnable both ad hoc and as a scheduled/gated step (e.g. from the refactor skill or a `wl doctor`-style hook), and is idempotent.
6. Tests: target deleted → `target-gone`; diagnostic fixed → `no-longer-reproduces`; diagnostic still firing → untouched; human-authored item → never touched; dry-run makes no writes.

## Scope note

The sweep itself belongs in this repository (`skill/refactor/`, and the audit side in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). If a worklog-level hook is preferred, that part belongs to the Worklog CLI project (`WL → /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`) and should be raised there — recorded as an assumption, not a decision.

## Impact

Stale, already-fixed findings stop inflating the backlog and stop being dispatched to agents, so the queue can be trusted to mean "work that still needs doing".
data.title: Linter-derived work items are never re-verified, so fixed and deleted-file findings stay open indefinitely

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 backlog review)

55 of the 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None of them surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

Deleting the parent recursively is the documented default (`wl delete` "Recursively deletes child items by default"), but `--no-recursive` exists ("leaving children orphaned") and a hard delete evidently bypassed the children — the exact route that produced the 46-item batch needs confirming as part of the fix.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Deleting a parent with open children either deletes them too, or refuses without an explicit `--force`/`--orphan-children` opt-in — **no silent orphaning**, including for hard deletes.
2. `wl doctor` reports orphaned children (parent id not resolvable) as a distinct finding, with the count, the lost-parent id and the child ids.
3. A documented remediation path with a **retention rule**: promote to top level (`wl update <id> --parent null`) when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is not (superseded, target gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered).
4. Both paths record a comment naming the previous parent and the decision, so the history is not lost.
5. Tests: delete-with-children rejects without force; `--no-recursive`/force orphaning is recorded; doctor output lists orphans; promotion clears `parentId` and keeps children reachable.

## Addendum - delete reasons are clobbered (observed 2026-11-08)

While retiring stale items during the backlog triage, `wl update <id> --delete-reason "<explanation>"` was applied first and `wl delete` then **overwrote** every one of them with the generic `deleted via wl delete`; the rationale had to be re-applied by a second `wl update` pass after deletion. 216 of the store's 847 pre-existing deletions carry that same uninformative string.

`wl delete` has no `--reason` option, so there is no supported way to record *why* an item is retired at the moment of retirement - exactly the audit trail a bulk cleanup needs.

**The defect is owned by the Worklog CLI project, not here:** it is filed as `WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7` (critical, open) with the full root-cause analysis, including the consequence that a hardcoded reason makes every CLI delete satisfy `isAttributedDelete()` (`src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:113`) and so bypasses the unattributed-delete protection from `WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO`. This item does **not** re-track it; the retirement workaround (re-apply reasons after deletion) is documented on `SA-0MW7Z1YE9004P41D`.

## Scope note

The guard and the doctor check belong to the **Worklog CLI** (`WL → /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), not to this repository, which only carries the data. Filed here because this is the worklog where the 55 orphans were found; migrate to the WL project if that is preferred. Recorded as an assumption.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.
data.title: Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py`'s integration verification (`_integrate_into_dev` /
`verifyIntegration`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) creates a fresh worktree with
`git worktree add --detach <path> <dev_sha>` and then runs `npm run build` in
it. `git worktree add` never populates git submodules, so any repository that
vendors a submodule builds against an **empty** submodule directory in the
integration worktree.

The build then fails with a module-resolution error, the audit marks any
execution-dependent AC (e.g. "Build and full test suite pass") as `partial`,
and the item's verdict is "Ready to close: No" — a **false negative**: the
real, populated checkout builds and tests green.

## Precedent (the fix already exists for implement worktrees)

`implement.py start` was fixed to populate submodules in new worktrees:
**SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ** (completed) added `_ensure_submodules(worktree_path,
repo_root)` running `git submodule update --init --recursive`, fail-open with a
warning. The audit skill's integration worktree should apply the same pattern;
today it does not.

Related: **SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6** (open) — audit should run its pipeline in a
fresh worktree at latest `origin/dev`; this item covers the submodule
population that fresh-worktree execution needs.

## Evidence (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising)

- Audit of `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` AC4: "Build fails (exit code 2) but errors
  are … missing vite config modules, **not from this item's changes**". The
  audit recognises the failure is environmental yet still blocks.
- On the real (populated) tree, `npm run build` exits **0**; the cached full
  suite is green.
- `vite.config.ts` imports from `./core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin`
  and `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`; `core/` is a tracked submodule.
- `git -c submodule.recurse=true worktree add --detach <tmp> <sha>` leaves
  `core/` with **0** entries (git 2.53.0) — `worktree add` does not recurse
  into submodules.
- `audit_runner.py` contains no `git submodule update --init` call.

## Desired change

After creating the integration worktree (and before `npm run build`), populate
tracked submodules — reuse/extract the `_ensure_submodules` helper pattern from
`implement.py` (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). Fail-open: a repo with no submodules must
be unaffected, and a submodule-init failure logs a warning without aborting the
audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The integration worktree used by `audit_runner.py` has its tracked
      submodules populated before `npm run build` (verified on a repo with a
      submodule dependency: the submodule directory is non-empty).
- [ ] `npm run build` in the integration worktree succeeds on a tree that
      builds green in the main checkout, so execution-dependent ACs are not
      marked `partial` for the empty-submodule reason.
- [ ] A repo without submodules is unaffected (fail-open); a submodule-init
      failure warns and does not abort the audit.
- [ ] A regression test covers the submodule-population step.

## Impact

Audits of build-dependent items on any submodule-vendoring repository reflect
the real tree, and releases stop being blocked by false-negative "not ready to
close" verdicts.

## Context

Discovered during the 2026-11-08 `/skill:ship release` of tce-the-rising, which
was blocked at the audit gate on `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` for this reason. The
per-project item filed there (`RISE-0MW7YP6SD0091MKJ`) is superseded by this
generic framework item and will be deleted.
data.title: Audit integration worktree does not populate git submodules, causing false-negative build verdicts

## Problem statement

During an audit, `audit_runner.py` transitions the target item out of
`completed`/`in_review` (to `in-progress`/`in_review` or `open`/`plan_complete`)
and is supposed to **restore it to `completed`/`in_review`** on every exit path
(the abort path logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`).

Under concurrency this restore is **lost**: a `wl sync` running in another
session (or the audit runner's own sync) races the restore, and the item is
left stuck at `open`/`plan_complete` (status `open`, stage `plan_complete`,
`auditResult: null`). The item silently drops out of the release candidate set
(`stage: in_review`) and looks like brand-new, un-implemented work — a
**worklog data-integrity regression**, not a cosmetic glitch.

This is the same class as the known concurrent-`wl sync` lost-update race
(WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); the audit runner's own status restore is not
race-safe against it.

## Observed (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising `/skill:ship release`)

A single release attempt corrupted **four** items, each left at
`open`/`plan_complete` although all four were `completed`/`in_review` before:

| Item | Corrupted by | Prior state (from worklog-data history) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RISE-0MVWWBT8Y009FMZ6` | release gate audit remediation (14:00) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3MXVU5009GMLR` | `--refresh-audits` (14:38) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:57) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:59) | `completed`/`in_review` |

All four were repaired by hand (`wl update <id> --status completed --stage
in_review`) after reconstructing the prior state from the `refs/worklog/...`
delta history. The corruption spans both the failing-verdict path (a
persisted "Ready to close: No" still left the item at `open`/`plan_complete`)
and the aborted path (the "restoring" message logged but the restore did not
persist).

## Root-cause hypotheses to confirm

- The restore is a plain `wl update` with no compare-and-swap / version guard,
  so a concurrent `wl sync` (pull→merge→push) overwrites it (last-writer-wins
  on a stale snapshot).
- A failing/aborted audit may not run the restore at all on some exit paths
  (the observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict
  suggests the restore is skipped when the verdict is not "Yes").

## Desired change

Make the audit runner's status restore **race-safe and unconditional**:

- Restore `completed`/`in_review` on **every** exit path — success, failing
  verdict, abort, exception, timeout — via `try/finally`.
- Use the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  and its claim/assignee handling so the restore participates in the same
  lost-update protection as other lifecycle exits.
- Guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (e.g. re-read after write,
  retry on mismatch — the same verification pattern the ship skill uses for
  close verification, SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- Never leave an item at `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed
  — a failing verdict is recorded while the item stays `completed`/`in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A failing audit verdict (Ready to close: No) leaves the item at
      `completed`/`in_review` with the verdict persisted — never `open`/`plan_complete`.
- [ ] An aborted audit (timeout / parse failure / provider error) restores the
      item to `completed`/`in_review`; the restore is verified after write and
      retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered it.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path (`try/finally`), including exceptions.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` (or a stale-snapshot
      write) between the audit's status change and its restore, and asserts the
      item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect of any audit
      path.

## Impact

Auditing an `in_review` item can no longer silently revert it to un-implemented
work, so release candidate sets and worklog state stay correct under
concurrent agent sessions.

## Context

Discovered during the 2026-11-08 `/skill:ship release` of tce-the-rising (four
items corrupted and repaired by hand). Related: the concurrent-`wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) and the ship close-verification pattern
(SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
data.title: Audit runner leaves items at open/plan_complete after a failing/aborted audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update)
